semantics.lagged: worker-originated router updates: KV cache events (indexer / overlap), prefill completion (mark_prefill_completed) and request completion (free) in the router's active-sequence load state
semantics.immediate: the router's own dispatch bookkeeping (add_request at admission), as in a live router that books what it routes; router-side prefill-token decay is a time model, not a signal
semantics.visibility: FIFO queue keyed by observed_ms + lag_ms; due updates are applied, in order, at the start of the first router callback (arrival, KV observation, prefill completion, request completion, topology change) at or after their visibility time, with slot updates stamped at the visibility time; if a load update was applied the router queue is drained then. There is no timer, so a queued request (router_queue_threshold, unused by the campaign's headline policies) is released at the next callback after its capacity becomes visible.
semantics.worker_removal: a removed worker's queued KV events are dropped (its lagged completions are no-ops after unregister)
semantics.scope: offline replay with router_mode kv_router (aggregated and disaggregated compositions). replay_mode online rejects lag > 0; round_robin ignores it (no router state).
semantics.lag_zero: lag 0 (or None) takes the pre-patch synchronous path

decision_level.note: routing_changed_frac = matched requests whose routing_workers differ from lag 0 (requests matched by session_id, turn, play, ISL, requested OSL); once one decision differs, later states diverge, so this is not a per-decision staleness rate

test_stage_usage: Use only the lag WT for the A5 pass: <lag WT>/.venv/bin/lr-eval --policy-spec FINALISTS --cells cells/test.jsonl --repeats 3 --router-state-lag-ms 0 50 200 --out runs/test/lag/results.jsonl, or on the CPU cluster <lag WT>/benchmarks/learned_routing/remote/submit_eval.sh --name test-lag-r1 --nodes N --repeats 3 --specs FINALISTS --cells cells/test.jsonl --router-state-lag-ms 0 50 200 --time HH:MM:SS, then the same WT's fetch_ingest.sh.
The lag-0 arm can be taken from this build (identical to the tuning build by the proof above) or from the headline test records; the 50/200 arms must come from this build.

Lag records carry build a6c6b04e and router_state_lag_ms; report them per lag (the lag WT's lr-report keeps lags apart; the tuning WT's report.py would pool lags of one build, so keep one lag per results file there).
round_robin ignores the lag (no router state), so its three lag arms are identical replays; it can be run at lag 0 only.

Do not rebuild the lag bindings: the bundle and records are tied to core_so 90464b9b. If the tuning branch changes evaluation code (HARNESS_VERSION bump) before the test stage, cherry-pick <commit-lag-01> onto it, rebuild, and re-run the lag-0 parity (runs/lag_patch/scripts/compare_lag.py).
LR-14 also suggests a 10 ms arm; the option takes any list (e.g. --router-state-lag-ms 0 10 50 200) at extra cost.
